analyzed_vuln.description: Heap out-of-bounds read occurs because IPv4Layer::toString() unconditionally calls getSrcIPv4Address()/getDstIPv4Address(), which directly dereference fields in iphdr (ipSrc/ipDst) without validating that the layer actually contains a full IPv4 header (>= sizeof(iphdr), 20 bytes). For truncated/fuzzed packets, an IPv4 layer object can exist with dataLen shorter than required for these fields, so getDstIPv4Address() reads past the packet buffer.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In FuzzTarget, attacker-controlled bytes are written to a pcap file and parsed into Packet layers. A malformed packet is parsed as IPv4 with insufficient captured bytes (ASan shows 28-byte packet buffer ending exactly where ipDst read occurs). Then parsedPacket.toString() / layer->toString() is invoked, reaching IPv4Layer::toString(). Because no length guard is performed before reading ipSrc/ipDst, a 4-byte read past allocation is triggered.
